We are asking that delegates bring something from their home territory or something that is special to them — a small jar of water from your lands, a book that is special to you, plant medicines, rocks, an article of clothing, a banner or flag from your community, a photo of your family, a cultural item or piece of jewellery. Please join us for a local walking tour: Please join us for a local walking tour of Gimuy (Cairns), hosted by local business Minjil. You'll receive a deep and rich understanding of local Bama culture in a unique and immersive experience. The tour begins with a smoking ceremony or welcome on the beach, followed by stories about Yidinydji Country and culture and the connection of other clans, families and tribes in the area. You'll also get the opportunity to try your hand at spear and boomerang throwing and taste some native teas and jams.

He is a celebrated Indigenous artist, author and educator, and a cornerstone of the Gimuy art community for more than 30 years. This hands-on workshop explores themes around rainforest and reef and is suitable for all ages and levels of experience. You'll be painting your own calico swag bag — the perfect memento to take home from your time spent with us.

Woven is a global initiative grounded in:
Woven is a global initiative grounded in the sacredness of ancestral knowledge, responsibilities, and aspirations. We steward projects and campaigns centered on climate action, land defense, and Indigenous rights and self-determination. Understanding that climate justice is interconnected with traditional culture, we create a space for Indigenous peoples to unite while celebrating regional differences.

Woven is the only global Indigenous organisation dedicated exclusively to advancing climate justice, and is guided by a Global Indigenous Advisory Council (GIAC) with Indigenous representatives from the UN Seven Sociocultural Regions of the world. The GIAC guides the project and ensures input from diverse global Indigenous voices.
Common Threads was launched in 2025 as a: Common Threads was launched in 2025 as an independent, non-profit organisation building national campaigns for truth, Treaties, land rights and climate justice — while providing support and resources to grassroots movements across the continent. We honour the leadership, knowledge and vision already held in communities and we work inclusively, backing collective action.

The Woven Project and Common Threads are:
The Woven Project and Common Threads are committed to creating a safe and inclusive experience at the Global Gathering for everyone, regardless of your gender, gender identity, sexual orientation, ethnicity, nationality, disability, physical appearance, body size, race, age, religion, economic status, immigration status or refugee status. We do not tolerate harassment of participants, staff or volunteers in any form, and any person who violates these rules may be removed from the event.

There is huge strength in our shared values and collective vision for the future, as well as strength in the diversity of our opinions, perspectives, experiences and approaches to creating change.

There is a responsibility on all of us to help create a space grounded in respect, care, and collective responsibility where everyone can speak, listen, learn, connect and belong. As such, we’ve developed a set of principles for how we show up in the space, alongside a code of conduct.

## Our Shared Commitments

By attending the Global Gathering, we agree to:

- Respect all identities, experiences and perspectives
- Listen — even in disagreements
- Create a safe place for ourselves and other delegates
- Prevent and speak out against any forms of lateral violence
- Hold space for others, especially unheard voices
- Protect the confidentiality of shared stories
- Contribute to a safe and inclusive environment

## How We Show Up

We agree to:

- Speak from your own experience
- Address ideas, not the person or people behind them
- Share space — be prepared to step up or step back
- Be mindful around accessibility and ensure everyone can participate

## Shared Responsibility

Creating this space is something we do together. Let’s show up with care, courage, and respect and make this a place where everyone has a place to belong. Common Threads staff are available throughout the summit if you need assistance, support or guidance.

## Reporting

To report any behaviour that makes you feel uncomfortable or unsafe, please reach out to Jai Deranger, our Wellbeing and Grievance Coordinator. You can also contact us at info@thewovenproject.org.
